options.text: It is based on con�icts and role disturbances seen in immediate environment
It is built on a hierarchy of goals
Hypothesis testing is carried out by the patient as home work
It is a structured therapy focussing on cognitive and emotional functioning along with reformulation

correct_answer.text: It is a structured therapy focussing on cognitive and emotional functioning along with reformulation

questions.explanation:
CAT combines Cognitive Theory and Psychoanalytical principles in therapy and encourages clients to draw on their ability to develop the
skills to change destructive patterns of behaviour. Negative ways of thinking are explored in structured and directive ways, involving diary-
keeping, reformulation letters, progress charts, etc. Retrieved from

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about Dialectical Behavioural Therapy?

options.text: It comprises of a hierarchy of goals
Low frustration tolerance is a contraindication
It is based on psychodynamic formulations

correct_answer.text: It comprises of a hierarchy of goals

questions.explanation:
DBT uses many principles of cognitive behaviour therapy (CBT), along with a strong emphasis on the use of acceptance strategies. DBT is a
dynamic and provocative treatment developed by Dr Marsha Linehan for patients with severe emotional dysregulation. One of the primary
concepts of dialectical behavior therapy is that self-harming behaviors are learned, and provide evidence of maladaptive coping that is
reinforced in an invalidating environment. Dialectical behavior therapy recommends a hierarchy of goals to e�ectively address the behaviors
associated with dysregulation (Retrieved from

questions.question_text: In multisystemic therapy, the treatment is usually given for a period of
questions.explanation:
In multisystemic therapy, the clinicians take on only four to six cases at a time, since the work is intensive. Treatment is usually given for
three months and then stopped.

questions.question_text: The target age range for functional family therapy in the treatment of conduct disorder is
questions.explanation:
One of the best-known interventions for serious antisocial behaviour is functional family therapy. It is designed to be practicable and
relatively inexpensive. The target age range is 11-18 years.

questions.question_text: Cognitive analytical therapy usually lasts for
questions.explanation:
A CAT therapy is weekly for 50-60 minutes sessions. A course of therapy can be from 16-24 sessions - this is negotiated with the therapist at
the start of therapy. Between one and �ve follow-up sessions are o�ered after the end of regular therapy. Again this is negotiated with the
therapist.

the onset of the symptoms. She also de�nes the problem as a medical illness and thus excuses the patient from self-blame. Which of the

options.text: A 55 year old man convicted for an impulsive sexual o�ence
A 14 year old boy with conduct disorder
A girl with the diagnosis of bulimia
A 66 year old woman with psychotic depression
A 45 year old man with a head injury

correct_answer.text: A girl with the diagnosis of bulimia

questions.explanation:
The description suits IPT - Inter-Personal Therapy. The focus for treatment includes events such as the death of someone important
(complicated bereavement), struggle with a signi�cant other (role dispute), or some other important life change (role transition); in the
relatively infrequent absence of any of these, the default focus is on interpersonal de�cits. IPT has good evidence base in support of treating

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is incorrect with respect to the principles of psychodynamic therapy?

options.text: Interpretation of the transference is the only means to access the unconscious mind
A therapist gains an insight of the client's issues by interpreting the unconscious motives
Worsening of symptoms is not uncommon during the course of psychodynamic therapy
Humans are instinctively irrational and destructive
Object loss can be associated with manic states

correct_answer.text: Interpretation of the transference is the only means to access the unconscious mind

questions.explanation:
In psychoanalytic psychotherapy the interpretation of the unconscious could be accessed through dreams, free-association (it is the
fundamental rule of psychoanalysis wherein the patient agrees to reveal everything that comes to mind during free association, no matter
how embarrassing or socially unacceptable), slips of the tongue and abreaction. Object loss is associated with both depression and manic
states. Both mania and depression are considered to be reactions to loss, may have no external basis in external reality and may be denied
in pathological grief. Worsening of symptoms is not uncommon during the course of psychodynamic therapy. It is referred to as negative
therapeutic reaction.

questions.question_text: Interpersonal therapy has been particularly used in the treatment of
questions.explanation:
IPT was developed in the 1970s by Klermann and Weissmann. It is a time-limited treatment that lasts for 12-16 hour long weekly sessions,
disorder focused which deals with symptoms in the 'here and now'. The focuses of treatment are the current interpersonal relationships and
their relationship to the development of illness. The focus is on role transitions like becoming a mother, job loss and role disputes like work
di�culties and relationship di�culties. IPT is indicated for the treatment of mild to moderate depressive illness, bulimia nervosa and
dysthymic disorder.

questions.question_text:
At the second session of psychodynamic psychotherapy, a distressed young woman says she dreamed she was sexually abused by her
father. What do you do?

options.text: Acknowledge her distress and ask if she was abused by her father
Explore the feelings it arouses in you
Ignore the comment and continue with the �ow the patient's talk
Leave it to the next session
Acknowledge her distress and ask her to talk about the dream

correct_answer.text: Acknowledge her distress and ask her to talk about the dream

questions.explanation: Acknowledging distress is an important aspect of therapeutic relationship across varying modalities of therapy.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following groups is particularly helpful for carers with mental illness?
questions.explanation: Carers �nd support groups particularly helpful.

questions.question_text: Eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing is a treatment for
questions.explanation:
When a trauma occurs, it seems to get locked in the nervous system with the original picture, sounds, thoughts and feelings. This material
can combine fact with fantasy and with images that stand for the actual emotions. The eye movements used in EMDR "unlock the nervous
system" (desensitise) and allow the brain to process correctly the experience (reprocessing) and is useful for treating established cases of
PTSD.

questions.question_text:
Which one among the following refers to the contents of the collective unconscious that describes a pancultural representation of human
experience?
questions.explanation:
Examples of pancultural representation of human experience (i.e. the Jungian archetypes) include the mother, the child, the hero, the self,
the shadow, anima and animus. 'Anima' refers to the unconscious feminine aspects of the male. 'Animus' refers to the unconscious
masculine aspects of the female. 'Shadow' refers to the unacknowledged aspects of oneself that includes both creative impulses and
destructive urges. 'Self' refers to the main archetype that gives the personality a sense of oneness. Persona refers to the outer concealed
aspects of oneself.

questions.question_text: Interpersonal therapy has been particularly useful in the treatment of which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal therapy is indicated in mild to moderate depressive illness and bulimia nervosa.

questions.question_text:
According to studies by Bateman and Fonagy, psychoanalytically oriented day hospital treatment has been shown to be superior to the
standard psychiatric treatment of patients with which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
An improvement in depressive symptoms, a decrease in suicidal and self-mutilation acts, reduced inpatient days, and better social and
interpersonal function was noted in borderline patients under partial hospitalisation program in an RCT.

questions.question_text: In which of the following therapies does positive transference get addressed early?
questions.explanation:
In brief dynamic therapy, a time limit is usually set in the beginning. The therapy lasts up to one year, usually 20-25 sessions. The techniques
employed include goal setting, focus choosing (identi�cation of currently active problems) and active involvement of the therapist in guiding
the therapy. The other features include addressing positive transference early on and addressing countertransference issues, working
through therapy termination.

questions.question_text: Which of the following predicts poor response to psychodynamic psychotherapy?

options.text: History of multiple acting out incidents

correct_answer.text: History of multiple acting out incidents

questions.explanation:
Lower socioeconomic status or average IQ need not be poor predictors of response by themselves. Multiple uncontrollable 'acting out'
incidents may predict recurrences and hence poor response to psychoanalysis.

questions.question_text: In psychoanalytic terms, condensation refers to

options.text: Combining various unconscious impulses into a single image while dreaming
Transfer of energy from an original object to a symbolic representation of the object
Representing abstract concepts by using recognisable images

correct_answer.text: Combining various unconscious impulses into a single image while dreaming

questions.explanation:
Condensation is a term used in dream analysis. It refers to the process of several unconscious impulses being combined into a single image
in the manifest dream content. e.g. One's father and a horrible teacher may be uni�ed and occur as a single dreadful monster in a child's
dream.

questions.question_text: Which of the following terms is the key principle in the work of therapeutic community?
questions.explanation:
Reality Confrontation: Patients continually have other people presenting interpretations of their behaviour, so defence mechanisms such as
denial, distortion and confusion become obvious. Over time, ongoing therapeutic interventions enable patients to re�ect on how they are
with other people, and to make changes. (Rapoport, 1960)

questions.question_text:
A middle-aged man with moderate depression is unwilling to take antidepressants but will have psychotherapy. Which factor would most
make you choose brief psychodynamic therapy?

options.text: History of one previous episode of depression
Wish to know more about self

correct_answer.text: Wish to know more about self

questions.explanation:
A wish to know more about oneself, the so-called psychological mindedness and a good degree of frustration tolerance are other positive
indicators to choose brief psychodynamic therapy.

questions.question_text:
Mr. Z has a history of acrophobia (fear of heights). Although he is terri�ed of heights, his long-term ambition in life was to become a pilot
and work for the air force. Which of the interventions given below is most likely to be successful for his condition?
questions.explanation:
Systematic Desensitisation (Wolpe): It consists of three steps: relaxation training, hierarchy construction, and desensitisation of the stimulus.
The patient is exposed to a graded hierarchy of anxiety-provoking situations in a stepwise fashion. Other behaviour therapy techniques
would include implosion (imaginal �ooding) and '�ooding'. In �ooding (in vivo) real life exposure takes place without any hierarchy. No
relaxation exercises are used. Escaping from an anxiety-provoking experience, in fact, reinforces the anxiety through avoidance
conditioning; in �ooding this conditioning is targeted. The success of �ooding depends on exposing patients for a reasonable duration until
mastery, and calm composure are gained. Premature withdrawal will reinforce the avoidance. In implosion (in vitro) or imaginal �ooding, the
phobic situation is confronted through imagination, not in real life. Ref: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry: Behavioural
Sciences/Clinical Psychiatry, 10th Edition. Lippincott Williams and Wilkins 2007

questions.question_text: Transactional analysis was �rst developed by
questions.explanation:
Eric Bern �rst developed transactional analysis (TA). TA has elements of psychoanalytic, humanist and cognitive approaches. It is considered
as a theory of personality and a systematic psychotherapy for personal growth and personal change.

questions.question_text: A depressed patient feels that only bad things happen to him. This is an example of
questions.explanation:
Catastrophisation refers to a speci�c, relatively innocuous event being read in cataclysmic proportions. Negative recall bias (only bad things
happen to me) is likely to be a selective abstraction.

questions.question_text: The best treatment option for bulimia nervosa is
questions.explanation:
Fairburn et al. describe transdiagnostic CBT as an 'enhanced' version of CBT that features 2 versions of the treatment: a 'focused' form which
focuses exclusively on the eating disorder and a 'broad' form which addresses some of the other issues commonly found in eating
disordered patients (e.g., self-esteem, perfectionism, interpersonal problems, mood intolerance).

questions.question_text: In major depressive disorder with comorbid personality disorder which of the following is true?

options.text: CBT has same e�cacy as IPT
Neither IPT nor CBT is useful

questions.explanation:
At least two studies have compared IPT with CBT head to head in patients with depression and comorbid personality disorders. Both
concluded that IPT was less e�ective than CBT in such comorbid presentations. But in general patients without axis two disorders respond
better to any form of psychotherapy for depression. (Rosenbluth, M et al. Depression and Personality p. 162).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about CBT is incorrect;

options.text: CBT is helpful for treatment of alcohol dependence
CBT and relaxation training are equally e�ective in generalized anxiety disorder
With homework tasks CBT produces quicker, longer lasting progression
CBT is better than waiting list in patients with HIV and depression
CBT is helpful for treatment of delusions

correct_answer.text: CBT and relaxation training are equally e�ective in generalized anxiety disorder

questions.explanation: There is good evidence for the e�ectiveness of CBT in anxiety disorder, HIV and depression, alcohol dependence and treatment of delusions.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a cognitive distortion?
questions.explanation: Arbitrary inference refers to quickly drawing a conclusion without the requisite evidence

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an accurate statement regarding humanistic psychotherapy?

options.text: Using therapeutic alliance as a supportive element for therapy

correct_answer.text: Using therapeutic alliance as a supportive element for therapy

questions.explanation:
Humanistic psychotherapy originally was promoted as a third force in psychotherapy. There is a great deal of importance placed on the
therapist-client relationship. Unlike other psychotherapies that view therapeutic relationship primarily as a means of delivering the
treatment, in humanistic therapy, the relationship itself is the treatment.

questions.question_text:
A couple sustained head on collision of their car but escaped with less than serious injuries. The husband does not want to discuss the
accident but su�ers from repeated nightmares and �ashbacks. He has stopped going to work since this happened. His wife is pursuing
insurance claims against the other driver. Which of the following could be a suitable treatment?

options.text: Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing Therapy

correct_answer.text: Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing Therapy

questions.explanation:
When a trauma occurs it seems to get locked in the nervous system with the original picture, sounds, thoughts and feelings. This material
can combine fact with fantasy and with 'images' that stand for the actual 'emotions'. The eye movements used in EMDR unlock the nervous
system (desensitise) and allow the brain to process correctly the experience (reprocessing).

questions.question_text:
A 19-year-old lady has a long-standing history of self-harm by taking overdoses and cutting herself in the past. She is impulsive, has low self-
esteem and has constant fears of abandonment. She also has a history of sexual abuse by her stepfather in the past. Which mode of
treatment is best recommended in this patient?
questions.explanation:
An RCT showed that DBT was superior to community-based treatment as usual' in women with BPD associated with repeated self-harm
(Linehan et al., 1991). Some bene�t was retained at follow-up (Linehan et al., 1993, 1994). A further study showed similar bene�ts in women
with BPD and substance misuse (Linehan et al., 1999) [Retrieved from

questions.question_text: Availability of the therapist for telephone contact between appointments is one of the approaches used in
questions.explanation:
Dialectical behavioural therapy (DBT) is an integrative therapy introduced in 1991 by Marsha Linehan and colleagues as a treatment for
borderline personality disorder, drawing on ideas from behavioural, cognitive and psychodynamic therapies. DBT speci�cally aims at
reduction of DSH and suicidal behaviour, improving the quality of life and personal relationships. DBT involves a variety of approaches:
individual therapy, group skills training and availability of the therapist for telephone contact between appointments.

questions.question_text: Carl Rogers was associated with
questions.explanation:
The therapy proposed by Carl Rogers is known as Patient/Client-centered therapy. The main aim of the therapist is to help the client
discover the distorted self-concepts that inhibit self-development. It is based on three cardinal principles- genuineness, accurate empathy
and unconditional positive regard

questions.question_text: Reformulation letters are characteristic features of
questions.explanation:
During CAT, by the third session, major maladaptive sequences and main reciprocal roles used by the patient are identi�ed. . Between the
third and fourth sessions the therapist writes a reformulation letter to the patient, which outlines the current situation and summarizes the
repertoire of reciprocal roles and procedural sequences used by the patient. In the penultimate session, the therapist gives the patient
another letter called goodbye letter that summarizes the therapy so far and outlines what remains to be achieved yet.

questions.question_text:
A child who is anxious about approaching dogs is repeatedly shown a dog when comfortably sitting on his mother's lap with an ice cream.
Gradually the anxiety reduces. The principle employed here is
questions.explanation: When anxiety and a relaxed state are co-existent, then anxiety reduces - this is called reciprocal inhibition.

questions.question_text: The major principles on which a therapeutic community is based includes all of the following except
questions.explanation:
The four major principles on which a therapeutic community is based are exempli�ed by the Henderson hospital model. According to this
model, the major components are (mnemonic CPD-R) 1. Communalism (Sta� are not separated from inmates by uniforms or behaviours,
mutual helping and learning occurs) 2. Permissiveness (tolerating each other and realising unpredictable behaviour can happen within the
community) 3. Democratisation (shared decision-making and joint running of the unit) and 4. Reality confrontation (self-deception or
distortions from reality are dealt with honestly and openly by all members without formalities).

questions.question_text:
Tolerating each other and realising unpredictable behaviour can happen within the community?. This statement de�nes which one of the
following principles of Therapeutic communities?
questions.explanation:
Rapoport explained the key features of TCs that included communalism, democracy, permissiveness and reality confrontation.
Permissiveness refers to tolerating each other and realising unpredictable behaviour can happen within the community.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is not a key feature of Therapeutic Community?
questions.explanation:
Therapeutic communities are one of the important and successful treatment options for personality disorders. The Henderson and Cassell
are well-known examples of therapeutic communities. In Henderson unit, the emphasis is on social analysis and in Cassell, psychoanalysis is
primary. Tom Main (coined the term therapeutic community), Maxwell Jones (established the therapeutic community) and Rapoport
explained the key features of TCs that includes communalism, democracy, permissiveness and reality confrontation.

questions.question_text:
A 40 yr old man with alcohol problems says that he has decided to quit drinking. He is ready to accept help and advice for this and
acknowledges the harm caused by alcohol. Which of the following stages of change is he in?
questions.explanation: He is in preparatory stages of Prochaska's model.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following terms refers to a patient's emotional attitude towards a therapist?
questions.explanation:
The development, in the patient, of feelings and patterns of behaviour towards the therapist, which unconsciously partly recapitulates
earlier relationships in their lives is known as transference. It usually takes a role earlier in the therapy and may even lead the patient to
resist the process. Countertransference describes the equivalent reaction in the therapist towards the patient. Both were initially considered
by Freud as hindrance to therapy. Parapraxis is a slip of the tongue commonly known as a Freudian slip. Occasionally it reveals unconscious
meaning, particularly in a�ect-laden situations. Interpretation refers to a formulation of current conscious problems in terms of unconscious
motives. It is also the expression of the therapist's understanding of the meaning of what is currently happening in therapy.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old dysthymic lady feels that every around her are depressed but she is not unhappy. What is the possible defence mechanism?
questions.explanation:
One way of disowning thoughts and feelings is to project them onto other people. We convince ourselves that those unpleasant thoughts
and feelings are coming from someone else and not from us.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following conditions in psychiatry was claimed to have insu�cient evidence to justify supporting the use of existing therapies in
practice?
questions.explanation:
Borderline personality disorder was claimed to have insu�cient evidence to justify supporting the use of existing therapies in practice such
as dialectical behaviour therapy, CBT, cognitive analytical therapy and mentalisation-based treatments.

questions.question_text: All of the following are principles of motivational interviewing except
questions.explanation: Expressing empathy, not sympathy, is a key process in motivational interviews.

questions.question_text: Klein's depressive position is related to the process of learning to cope with which of the following con�icts?
questions.explanation:
Melanie Klein described two positions - paranoid-schizoid and depressed position. The paranoid-schizoid position is associated with the use
of splitting and projection as a defence mechanism. This position concerns an inability to perceive a whole object and splits all objects into
their good and bad parts. But in the depressive position, the infant tolerates the ambiguity or ambivalence and can realise that an individual
can have both good and bad qualities. In paranoid-schizoid position, the anxiety is about the survival of the self but in depressive position
the anxiety is about the loss of the object.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a technique used in DBT?
questions.explanation:
The four modes of treatment in DBT are (1) group skills training, (2) individual therapy, (3) phone consultations, and (4) consultation team.
Role transitions are managed in interpersonal therapy.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following statements about dream work is true?

options.text: Dreams are always interpreted in psychoanalytic psychotherapy
The dream work involves conversion of latent content into manifest content.
Dream work converts the manifest content of the dream into its latent content
Primary process thinking does not occur in dreaming
The mental mechanisms involved in the psychoanalytic therapy of dreams include primary elaboration

correct_answer.text: The dream work involves conversion of latent content into manifest content.

questions.explanation:
According to Freud, dreams are the royal road to the unconscious. In dreams, Freud distinguished between latent content (unconscious
feelings that include the wishes, anxieties and fantasies) and manifest content ( recalled dream). The dream work involves conversion of
latent content into manifest content.

questions.question_text: Cognitive analytical therapy was developed by which one of the following therapists?
questions.explanation:
Cognitive-analytic therapy (CAT) is a brief focal therapy informed by cognitive therapy, psycho- dynamic psychotherapy and certain
developments in cognitive psychology. Anthony Ryle developed CAT speci�cally in response to the need for treatment approaches of short
duration in the National Health Service (NHS).

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is least used technique in CBT
questions.explanation:
The paradoxical injunction is a term used in family therapy. The therapist makes the patient intentionally engage in the unwanted behaviour
(called the paradoxical injunction), e.g., avoid a phobic object or perform a compulsive ritual. This counterintuitive approach can provide new
insight for some patients.

questions.question_text:
An 18-year-old girl with relapse of bulimia is found to have poor engagement with the treating team. The most suitable psychological
therapy would be
questions.explanation:
Interpersonal therapy (IPT) has been identi�ed as an e�ective treatment for bulimia nervosa that does not focus on bulimic symptoms.
Rather, a detailed assessment culminating in an 'interpersonal inventory' identi�es core associated interpersonal problem(s) that become
the focus of treatment.

questions.question_text: Choose the �rst step in treating a patient who is afraid of spiders and avoids them:
questions.explanation: Taking a detailed history to establish the diagnosis is the most important step.

questions.question_text: Choose the most accurate statement about Interpersonal Therapy?

options.text: Focus is on social skills development
Attempts to explain psychoanalytic ideas in cognitive terms
Aim is to extinguish maladaptive behaviour and substitute more adaptive ones
Empower patients to make use of their own strengths
Therapy focuses on the 'here and now'

correct_answer.text: Therapy focuses on the 'here and now'

questions.explanation:
Interpersonal therapy is a practical short-term, time-limited, 'here and now' therapy. Emotional problems are best understood by studying
the interpersonal context (ongoing/current situation) in which they arise.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a technique used in psychodynamic psychotherapy?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement (positive or negative) is a technique used in behavioural psychotherapy - not psychodynamic psychotherapy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a relative contraindication to brief time-limited psychotherapeutic approach?

options.text: Having simple and speci�c problems to be addressed
Good ability to form trusting relationships

questions.explanation: Chronic maladaptive patterns tend to be deeply wired and need longer therapies.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following, if present, reduces the suitability of a patient for psychoanalytic psychotherapy?

options.text: Ability to form and sustain relationships

questions.explanation:
Poor frustration tolerance and impulsivity seen in antisocial PD are among the factors indicating poor suitability for psychoanalytic modes of
therapy.

questions.question_text: What predicts a poor response to psychodynamic psychotherapy?

options.text: Good impulse control and good frustration tolerance
Patient can understand things in psychological terms

questions.explanation:
Repeated uncontrolled self-harm can interfere signi�cantly with the psychotherapy. In general, such patients are not suitable for a
psychodynamic approach.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a cognitive technique used in CBT?
questions.explanation:
The overall purpose of Socratic questioning is to challenge accuracy and completeness of thinking in a way that acts to move people towards
their ultimate goal.

questions.question_text: Interpersonal therapy does not focus on one of the following areas.
questions.explanation:
Examples of areas covered are disputes with friends, family or co-workers, grief and loss and role transitions, such as retirement or divorce.
Attachment issues are not dealt in IPT.

questions.question_text: Unconditional positive regard is a feature of
questions.explanation:
Client-centred therapy by Carl Rogers emphasises the importance of therapeutic attributes of genuineness, unconditional positive regard
and accurate empathy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following therapies use 'mindfulness' as a therapeutic strategy?
questions.explanation: Core mindfulness training i.e. learning to monitor internal mental states, is a characteristic feature of DBT.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a self-rating scale?
questions.explanation:
Self-rating scale-Beck depression inventory, hospital anxiety and depression scale and Zung depression rating scale. Observer rating scales-
Hamilton rating scale for depression, Montgomery Asberg depression rating scale, Young Mania Scale and Yale-brown obsessive compulsive
scale.

questions.question_text: Which of the following predicts poor treatment response in chronic fatigue syndrome when treated with CBT/graded exercise?
questions.explanation:
Predictors of poor outcome when treating CFS include (Powell et al, 2004) 1. claiming a disability related bene�t 2. low sense of control 3.
strong focus on physical symptoms 4. being passive with reduced activity and 5. membership of self help group (Note: this does not mean
that self help groups worsen CFS; membership may be an indicator of perceived severity)

questions.question_text: Defence mechanisms are a function of the
questions.explanation:
The �rst systematic account of defence mechanisms was written by Freud's daughter Anna Freud in the book 'Ego and the Mechanisms of
Defence' in 1936.
